definitions.explanation: The geological process of land rising or being pushed upward, or the resulting elevated landform.
A raised area on a surface, including on the body. Used in medical and general descriptive contexts.

examples.english: The road has cracks due to the ground swelling up.

notes:
A compound of {隆|りゅう} (to rise; prominent) and {起|き} (to rise; to occur). Most commonly encountered in geology and earth science, but also used in medicine and anatomy. Japan's volcanic and seismic geography makes this a relatively common word in news reporting.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {隆起|りゅうき}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to be uplifted; to rise; to swell
- ⟦{地殻|ちかく}→地殻：12142_chikaku⟧{隆起|りゅうき}: crustal uplift
- {隆起|りゅうき}サンゴ⟦{礁|しょう}→礁：25212_shou⟧: uplifted coral reef
- ⟦{海底|かいてい}→海底：13287_kaitei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{隆起|りゅうき}: seabed uplift
- {隆起|りゅうき}⟦{部|ぶ}→〜部：00440_bu⟧: protuberance; raised area

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{沈降|ちんこう}→沈降：23104_chinkou⟧: subsidence — the opposite process; land sinking down
- {膨|ふく}らみ: swelling; bulge — a softer, everyday term for something that puffs up
- {突起|とっき}: protrusion; projection — a sharp or pointed raised part
